episodes.184488: Severe storms developed over portions of eastern NM. One strong storm dropped nickel sized hail in Colfax County in the afternoon. Later in the evening, two severe storms produced strong wind gusts at the Tucumcari and Roswell airport observing sites.
episodes.184637: Moist mid-levels, a surface pressure trough, and strong surface heating allowed for thunderstorms to develop in eastern New Mexico by late afternoon. Storms slowly moved into the South Plains of West Texas through the evening. High winds associated with a strong outflow boundary occurred near Sundown as measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet. Very dry sub-cloud layers allowed one of these storms to produce a severe wind gust at Reese Center (Lubbock County). After thunderstorms moved through Lubbock County, a wake low developed which produced several high wind gusts across Lubbock County.||Peak wind gusts reported by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet are listed below:||59 mph at Shallowater (Lubbock County), and|59 mph at Lubbock Christian University (Lubbock County).||A peak wind gust of 62 mph was reported by the Automated Surface Observing System at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport.
episodes.184910: Gusty winds were observed in many locations around Utah as precipitation began ahead of an approaching system.
episodes.185077: A weak upper-level short-wave helped initiate clustered storms in a line along a cold front on the evening of September 29. The individual clustered storms merged over Madison, Stanton, and Wayne counties. There were several 1-inch hail reports a few wind reports. The strongest measured wind gust was 78 mph at the Wayne Airport. Wind gusts led to tree damage and downed power lines in that tri-county area.
episodes.185410: Two waves of thunderstorms in central Minnesota produced significant wind damage. A brief EF-0 tornado occurred near Rockford, MN in Wright County during the first wave of storms. The strongest estimated thunderstorm gusts were around 75-80 mph given the nature of the observed wind damage.
episodes.185578: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms interacting with a stalled frontal boundary to the north over central Florida produce a waterspout southeast of Saint James City in Lee County.
episodes.185579: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms interacting with a stalled frontal boundary to the north over central Florida produce heavy rain and street flooding near North Port in Sarasota County.
episodes.185675: A complex of thunderstorms collapsed across southeast New Mexico and the western Permian Basin. This resulted in localized strong to severe outflow winds.
episodes.186065: The month of September concluded with thunderstorms that brought heavy rain, rockslides, high elevation mountain snow, and a funnel cloud report.
episodes.186148: A cold front brought active weather into parts of northern California and western Nevada mostly north of US-50 during this period. A 15-20% chance for isolated thunderstorms A narrow band of showers along a cold front passage overnight Friday into Saturday morning was followed by a 15-20% chance for isolated thunderstorms Saturday afternoon. Then intermittent bands of valley rain/mountain snow showers followed later Saturday night through early Sunday morning.
episodes.186185: Heavy rainfall led to flooding in Ormond Beach in Volusia County.

events.narrative: A storm survey determined damaging winds accompanied a brief tornado. The damaging winds were offset south and east of the tornado path. At least two dozen trees were downed.

A brief tornado touched down just south of the intersection of Wright County Road 14 and 30th Street Southeast. The tornado tracked northeast and mainly uprooted or broke over 100 trees, most of them at one farmstead. A storm survey was conducted and maximum winds were estimated at 85 mph.

A downburst hit a large area southeast and east of Buffalo, MN. The storm survey found a path that was just over four miles long and which broadened out as the downburst moved to the northeast. Hundreds of trees were downed, mostly to the northwest, north, and northeast. Some trees fell on sheds, garages, and vehicles. Multiple farm buildings suffered major damage. A large window in a house was blown inward. A double garage door was blown in and soffit from an adjacent barn was blown off. The last of the surveyed damage was to a park and farm on the southern shore of Beebe Lake. At the farm, winds blew in the south wall of a machine shed which landed on a combine. Portions of this shed were found nearly 300 yards to the northwest.
